q-109537.name: Question 1
q-109537.problem: Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points $(-3,-1)$ and $(4,2).$
q-109537.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the point $(-3,-1),$ so we can use $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-3,-1)$ in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute $m,$ and we can do this using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{2-(-1)}{4-(-3)}=\frac{2+1}{4+3}=\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=\frac{3}{7}$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-3,-1)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-1) & =\frac{3}{7}(x-(-3)) \\ y+1 & =\frac{3}{7}(x+3)\end{aligned}
$$

q-109537.html:
Question 1
?

Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points (−3,−1) and (4,2).

a
y+1=37(x+3)
b
y+3=3(x+1)
c
y−1=37(x+3)
d
y+3=37(x−1)
e
y−1=3(x−3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We know that the line passes through the point (−3,−1), so we can use (x1,y1)=(−3,−1) in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute m, and we can do this using the given points:

m=y2−y1x2−x1=2−(−1)4−(−3)=2+14+3=37

Then, we substitute m=37 and the point (x1,y1)=(−3,−1) into the point-slope formula:

y−y1=m(x−x1)y−(−1)=37(x−(−3))y+1=37(x+3)

q-109542.name: Question 2
q-109542.problem: Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points $(-1,4)$ and $(5,2).$
q-109542.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the point $(-1,4),$ so we can use $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,4)$ in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute $m,$ and we can do this using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{2-4}{5-(-1)}=\frac{-2}{6}=-\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=-\frac{1}{3}$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-1,4)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{1}{3}(x-(-1)) \\ y-4 & =-\frac{1}{3}(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

q-109573.problem: Calculate the equation of the line that passes through the points $(-5,3)$ and $(-1,-1).$
q-109573.worked_solution:
First, we will construct the point-slope formula for the line. Then, we will simplify the point-slope formula into slope-intercept form.

We start by computing the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{-1-3}{-1-(-5)}=\frac{-4}{4}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=-1$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-5,3)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-3 & =-(x-(-5)) \\ y-3 & =-(x+5)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the equation into slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-3 & =-(x+5) \\ y-3 & =-x-5 \\ y & =-x-2\end{aligned}
$$

q-109573.html:
Question 3
?

Calculate the equation of the line that passes through the points (−5,3) and (−1,−1).

a
y=−x−2
b
y=−x+7
c
y=x−2
d
y=−x−7
e
y=x+3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we will construct the point-slope formula for the line. Then, we will simplify the point-slope formula into slope-intercept form.

We start by computing the slope m using the given points: m=y2−y1x2−x1=−1−3−1−(−5)=−44=−1

Then, we substitute m=−1 and the point (x1,y1)=(−5,3) into the point-slope formula: y−y1=m(x−x1)y−3=−(x−(−5))y−3=−(x+5)

Finally, we simplify the equation into slope-intercept form:

y−3=−(x+5)y−3=−x−5y=−x−2
